positions.stakeholder_concern: The commenter finds FDA's two-axis activity-by-consequence risk framework useful but asserts it cannot serve as a complete measure on its own, noting that FDA itself raises reversibility, downstream safeguards, time pressure, and traceability, and that other sections of the paper implicate further factors (user review capability, conversational trajectory, escalation direction, benchmark validity, subgroup behavior, third-party model change, postmarket detectability, and agentic tool use).
positions.requested_fda_action: Expand the risk framework beyond the two axes by incorporating the additional dimensions identified, which the commenter would operationalize as a 15-driver 'boundary budget' and material coupling screen.
positions.source_passage: The central BCR finding is that FDA's two-axis activity-by-consequence picture is useful but cannot serve as the complete closure observable. FDA itself asks whether reversibility, downstream safeguards, time pressure, and traceability should also be represented. Other sections add user review capability, conversational trajectory, escalation direction, benchmark validity, subgroup behavior, third-party model change, postmarket detectability, and agentic tool use. BCR converts these into a 15-driver boundary budget and material coupling screen.

positions.stakeholder_concern: The commenter warns of 'benchmark false-lock' — that benchmark performance could be treated as automatic safety closure despite FDA's own acknowledgment of contamination, saturation, and limited real-world representativeness of public benchmark assets.

representativeness of public benchmark assets. BCR therefore treats benchmark performance as one witness, never as
automatic safety closure. The repair chain is benchmark construct validity -> independent/sequestered testing -> clinical
confirmation -> postmarket residual monitoring -> automatic re-open after safety-relevant change.

positions.source_passage: Meaningful human oversight is not yet reduced to measurable visibility, authority, intervention time, override, and reversibility criteria.

positions.stakeholder_concern: The commenter observes that while the discussion paper acknowledges benchmark construct validity as a problem, it does not establish a required, closed chain of evidence linking benchmark performance to clinical confirmation and then to observed postmarket behavior.
positions.requested_fda_action: Close the evidentiary chain by requiring a demonstrated linkage from benchmark results through clinical confirmation to postmarket performance, rather than treating construct validity only as an acknowledged concern.
positions.source_passage: Benchmark construct validity is recognized as a problem but a mandatory proof chain from benchmark -> clinical confirmation -> postmarket behavior is not closed.

positions.stakeholder_concern: The passage notes only that the selection of a clinical confirmation approach is left open-ended and that there is no deterministic rule for escalating to a more rigorous confirmation method when residual uncertainty is unresolved; it does not state support for or opposition to the described framework.
positions.requested_fda_action: Implicitly, that FDA specify a determinate escalation rule or criteria governing when a more rigorous clinical confirmation approach is required for unresolved residual uncertainty; the passage does not spell out a specific requested action.
positions.source_passage: Clinical confirmation selection remains open and lacks a deterministic escalation rule for unresolved residuals.

positions.stakeholder_concern: The passage asserts that there is no closed rule governing independence or transportability when synthetic and real-world evidence are combined, implying uncertainty about when such pooling is statistically defensible. It does not state whether the commenter supports or opposes the discussion paper's approach.
positions.requested_fda_action: No explicit request is stated; the passage only identifies the absence of a defined independence/transportability rule for combining synthetic and real evidence.
positions.source_passage: Synthetic/real evidence combination lacks a closed independence/transportability rule.

positions.stakeholder_concern: The passage notes only that requirements for third-party model identity/change detection and hold-or-rollback capability are not currently mandatory, identifying this as a gap in controls over third-party foundation model changes.
positions.requested_fda_action: No explicit request is stated; the passage at most implies that such detection and hold/rollback requirements could be made mandatory rather than optional.
positions.source_passage: Third-party model identity/change detection and hold/rollback requirements are not yet mandatory.

positions.stakeholder_concern: The commenter observes that current PCCP concepts lack expression as a measurable boundary or delta envelope, implying that permissible modification limits for GenAI-enabled devices are not quantifiable as presently articulated.
positions.requested_fda_action: Appears to ask FDA to translate PCCP change-control concepts into measurable boundaries (a quantified 'delta envelope') for allowable post-deployment modifications; the brief passage does not specify further detail.
positions.source_passage: PCCP concepts are not yet expressed as a measurable boundary-delta envelope.

positions.stakeholder_concern: The commenter indicates that evaluation of agentic GenAI-enabled devices lacks explicit requirements covering action state, tool permissions, irreversible action points, and verification after actions are taken.
positions.requested_fda_action: Require explicit evaluation elements for agentic devices, specifically action-state tracking, tool-permission controls, identification of irreversible nodes, and post-action verification.
positions.source_passage: Agentic evaluation needs explicit action-state, tool-permission, irreversible-node, and post-action verification requirements.

positions.stakeholder_concern: The commenter indicates that postmarket monitoring as described lacks defined ownership of residual risk, explicit trigger thresholds, harm-timing logic, and mechanisms for automatic re-opening or requalification.
positions.requested_fda_action: Require that postmarket monitoring frameworks specify residual owners, trigger thresholds, harm-time logic, and automatic re-open/requalification mechanisms.
positions.source_passage: Postmarket monitoring needs residual owners, trigger thresholds, harm-time logic, and automatic re-open/requalification.

positions.stakeholder_concern: The commenter regards the discussion paper as a strong starting point but treats its open questions as unresolved, holding that the policy concept remains only 'PARTIAL' until proposed controls are implemented and empirically demonstrated.
positions.requested_fda_action: Convert the paper's open questions into a traceable realization-and-closure architecture and require that the proposed controls be implemented and empirically demonstrated before the policy concept is treated as complete.
positions.source_passage: Final BCR conclusion. FDA's discussion paper is a strong starting point. BCR does not reject it; BCR converts the open questions into a traceable realization-and-closure architecture. The policy concept remains PARTIAL until the proposed controls are implemented and empirically demonstrated.
